source: spec/transport-adapter.md TA-1, TA-4, TA-6; draft-ietf-moq-transport-22 §9.1.1 (AUTHORITY), §9.1.2 (PATH); URL serialisation per the WHATWG URL Standard
note: The setup options the core adds to CLIENT_SETUP for the endpoint, by framing. `url` is the endpoint the caller passes. `token` is what getToken returns; absent means no getToken. `framing` is what the transport factory declares; absent means it declares nothing, which is a WebTransport session. `path` and `authority` are the exact UTF-8 values of PATH (0x01) and AUTHORITY (0x05); null means the option MUST NOT be sent. The token reaches PATH through the URL's jwt query parameter, so its encoding is the URL Standard's application/x-www-form-urlencoded serialiser.

cases.name: a factory that declares no framing sends neither option
a WebTransport session sends neither option
QMux over WebSocket sends neither option: the upgrade request carries the URL
native QUIC carries the endpoint path and the token from getToken
native QUIC keeps the endpoint query and form-encodes the token after it
native QUIC carries an explicit jwt exactly as given
native QUIC with no token sends the path without a query
native QUIC keeps an explicitly empty query
native QUIC with an empty endpoint path sends the root path
native QUIC keeps a percent-encoded path segment encoded
native QUIC includes a non-default port in the authority
native QUIC omits the default port from the authority
